summary: This program builds a small list of farmers' market products, prints the whole inventory, and then uses a stream pipeline to pull out the names of organic summer items ordered from cheapest to most expensive.

lines.text: Comparator supplies the ready-made comparison objects that a stream's sorted step needs in order to know what "in order" means.
Collectors holds the factory methods that turn a finished stream back into an ordinary collection, such as a List.
The variable is declared with the List interface but created as an ArrayList, so the rest of the code depends only on general list behaviour.

lines.code: products.add(new MarketProduct("Heirloom Tomatoes", "Sunny Fields Farm", 4.50, "Produce", "Summer", true));
lines.text: Each product is constructed with its name, vendor, price, category, season, and an organic flag, giving the stream several fields to filter and sort on.

lines.code: products.add(new MarketProduct("Wildflower Honey", "Bee Kind Apiary", 12.00, "Honey", "Late Summer", true));
lines.text: The season here is "Late Summer" rather than "Summer", which is exactly why the filter later searches for the word inside the text instead of testing for equality.
An enhanced for loop walks the whole inventory so the reader can see the raw data before any stream filtering happens.
Concatenating an object onto a string calls its toString method, so each product prints in whatever readable form MarketProduct defines.
The query is kept in its own method, so main stays about setting up data and reporting results.
Calling stream turns the list into a pipeline of elements that the following steps can filter, sort, and transform without changing the original list.

The lambda keeps only products that pass every test: organic, with a season that exists, and whose season text mentions summer in any capitalisation. The null check comes before the method call so a missing season cannot cause an exception.
comparingDouble builds a comparator from the price getter, arranging the surviving products from lowest price to highest.
The method reference replaces each MarketProduct in the pipeline with its name, so the stream changes from a stream of products to a stream of strings.
The terminal operation gathers the results into a new List<String>, preserving the sorted order the pipeline produced.
